validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real, well-documented proposal, distinct from every other roster row. Feb 2019: Pakistan's Inter State Gas Systems (ISGS, state-owned) and Russia's Gazprom PJSC signed an inter-corporate agreement (following a June 2018 MOU) for a >1,500 km, $10bn UNDERSEA/offshore gas pipeline landing at Gwadar, part of a wider $14bn Gazprom package that also covered the separate Pakistan Stream / North-South line ($2.5bn) and gas storage ($1.5bn). Corroborated independently by thenews.com.pk (7-Feb-2019, the sheet's own already-cited Length/SegmentCost source, recovered via Wayback since the live page now 403s), Russia Business Today, Warsaw Institute (two separate articles, 2019 and 2022), Asia Times (Jul-2019), Gulf Times, and Profit/Pakistan Today (Jun-2018) -- all independent outlets, all describing the SAME $10bn/1,500km/Gwadar project, not a wire reprint. CLASSIFICATION: Fuel=Gas and PipelineType=transmission are both correct -- every source describes a large trunk import line, not a gathering/process line. DUPLICATE: checked against the full 6-row Pakistan-gas roster. NOT the same pipe as P3101 (Pakistan Stream/North-South: $2.5bn, ~1,100-1,122 km, Karachi Port Qasim -> Lahore/Kasur, onshore) -- every source treats the offshore project and Pakistan Stream as two separate line items in the same Gazprom package, with different costs and different lengths, and even mentions a possible future 'sea link' BETWEEN the two (Warsaw Institute, Sep-2022) that confirms they are not the same object. NOT the same pipe as P0452 (the classic onshore Iran-Pakistan 'Peace' pipeline, Asaluyeh->Sindh, 2,775 km) -- P3174 is the Gazprom-brokered undersea ALTERNATIVE route via Gwadar (Asia Times, Jul-2019: 'the gas volume allocated for the IP gas pipeline project would be diverted to the offshore gas pipeline project'), a materially different length/cost/sponsor. ATTRIBUTION CAVEAT (the one real finding): sources disagree on which country's gas actually feeds the pipeline. Warsaw Institute (x2), Asia Times, and Gulf Times all name IRAN as (at least one of) the source country/fields, matching the sheet's current EndCountryOrArea=Iran. But the earliest, most specific, on-the-record report -- thenews.com.pk, 7-Feb-2019, quoting the signing officials directly, and already cited by the sheet for Length/SegmentCost -- states the gas would come from 'Gazprom's sources in the Middle East,' naming 'Bahrain, Qatar and other Middle Eastern countries' and never mentioning Iran. Gulf-Times splits the difference ('gas deposits in Iran and in other Middle East countries'). So 'Iran' has more independent naming instances (3 outlets) than 'Qatar/Bahrain' (1 outlet, albeit the most authoritative direct-quote piece), but no single source is unambiguous and none of this ever reached a final, sourced route -- flag as an open attribution question rather than a settled fact. SPEC: Length 1,500 km confirmed verbatim by 2 independent sources (thenews.com.pk: 'more than 1,500 km'; Russia Business Today: 'over 1,500 km'). Cost $10bn confirmed by 5+ independent sources. Capacity 1000 MMcf/d matches the upper end of the range every source gives ('500 million to one billion cubic feet of gas per day') -- consistent, not contradicted. OWNER: Gazprom PJSC is correctly named as the Russian corporate counterpart (thenews.com.pk names the signatory as 'Vitaly A Markelov ... PJSC Gazprom International'), but the recorded Owner1%=100.00% is an unconfirmed convention value -- this MOU never reached FID and no equity/ownership structure for an actual pipeline entity has ever been announced (contrast with Pakistan Stream/P3101, where a 74%/26% Pakistan/Russia split IS reported). STATUS OF THE STATUS REF: the sheet's Status[ref] (warsawinstitute.org 'Russia Enters the Pakistan Gas Sector') is live (200) and does substantively support 'proposed'/feasibility-stage even though it doesn't contain the literal word 'proposed' -- the worklist's automated flag on this is a false negative, not a real support gap.

fills.researcher_notes: Both sources state Pakistan would import '500 million to one billion cubic feet of gas per day (MMCFD)' -- the recorded 1000 MMcf/d is the stated upper bound of the range, not a contradiction. Live thenews.com.pk page now 403s (anti-bot); recovered via Wayback per standing rule (kept alongside, not swapped in).

Gazprom PJSC is confirmed as the Russian corporate counterpart to Pakistan's ISGS on this project (thenews.com.pk names the signatory 'Vitaly A Markelov ... PJSC Gazprom International'). The 100.00% equity share is NOT independently confirmed by any source -- this is a pre-FID feasibility-study MOU with no announced ownership/equity structure for an actual pipeline entity. Tier held to medium and the % is flagged as a convention placeholder rather than a sourced fact; recommend a ResearcherNotes caveat rather than removing the ref.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Timeline of real progress: Jun-2018 MOU -> Feb-2019 inter-corporate agreement -> Gazprom's feasibility study originally slated to START Q1-2020 and finish within one year (Gulf Times). No source anywhere reports feasibility-study results, a financing close, or any construction milestone for THIS specific offshore/undersea project. The most recent substantive mention found is Warsaw Institute, 30-Sep-2022, which says only that 'a sea link between the offshore pipeline and the Pakistan Stream gas pipeline is now being considered' -- i.e. still speculative, no progress. A Feb-2023 Pipeline Technology Journal piece on reviving the North-South/Pakistan Stream project via Gwadar mentions an 'abandoned Gwadar LNG Pipeline Project' connecting to Iran, run by ISGS + Chinese firms -- this appears to be a RELATED BUT DISTINCT entity (an LNG-import + onshore pipe concept, not clearly the same as Gazprom's $10bn undersea line), so I have not merged it in, but it reinforces that the broader 'Gwadar seaborne gas import' concept had stalled by 2023. Broader Pakistan-Russia energy news through 2024-2025 (e.g. Gazprom/Novatek LNG talks, Portovaya/Ust-Luga LNG cooperation) has shifted entirely to LNG supply rather than this pipeline, with no mention of the offshore line being revived. Iran's own onshore IP pipeline (P0452) was separately reported abandoned by Pakistan in Aug-2023 over US-sanctions risk (Middle East Monitor), removing much of the rationale for an Iran-sourced offshore alternative too. With no independent evidence of activity since ~Sep-2022 (roughly 4 years dormant as of Aug-2026), the 2-year proposed-with-no-progress dormancy rule applies: propose Status=shelved, ShelvedCancelledType=Presumed, no fabricated ref per standing rule 2.

summary: P3174 (Off-Shore Gas Pipeline) is real and correctly classified/not a duplicate -- length (1,500 km), cost ($10bn), and capacity (up to 1,000 MMcf/d) all independently corroborated across 6+ outlets; one attribution caveat (sources split between Iran and Qatar/Bahrain as the gas source country) and one unconfirmed Owner1% (100%, pre-FID placeholder). Status proposed to change proposed->shelved (Presumed) on ~4y dormancy, no evidence found past Sep-2022.
